checks.method: Reopened the primary H27 decision problem, equation 6.13, Lemma 6.6, Proposition 6.7 and computational verification; compared the prior preprint’s explicit import.
checks.observation: [H27](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06175v1) derives support at most 85 for a hypothetical 28-member intersecting family; its 128-column capacity exceeds that bound. The unrestricted theorem statement matches the manuscript. Section 6.5 distinguishes exhaustive searches from completed-record verification. The [prior preprint](https://aixiv.online/abs/2610.01292) explicitly imports H27 without rerunning it. Historical execution authentication remains unverified here.
checks.scope: Challenge: H27 conceals a support cutoff or gains spurious corroboration

checks.method: Reopened both versioned primary records; evaluated the later theorem’s explicit bound using exact rational arithmetic and read its Section 5 limitations.
checks.observation: The prior v1 still states maximum 68 and explicitly excludes any claim to exclude size 68. [Bucić–He–Lee, Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.26686v1) gives 3(863/432)^n for three petals. A 68-member simple four-uniform family needs n≥8; this bound already exceeds 760 there and increases. Their vector bound remains alphabet-dependent. Thus this direct competitor does not yield 67; this is not exhaustive exclusion of all possible derived corollaries or unlocated work. Reopening sources does not extend the manuscript’s search cutoff.
checks.scope: Challenge: a later general result already subsumes upper 67

checks.method: Compared committed Alpha’s identified interface directly with pinned main.tex lines 1003–1024 and LOW14-NO43-ordinary-closure’s matching and cross-star sections.
checks.observation: The source requires both centres outside both actual tail supports. The new proof separately excludes Q8 leaf overlap using an actual two-edge matching, then uses an opposite core member to establish cross-intersection of the 8+8 tails. The resulting bound is 14+14−1+4=31<41. Core isolation alone would fail this guard, but the additional argument is present. This inspects the import bridge, not every prior certificate.
checks.scope: Challenge: the cap14 closure borrows an invalid prior cross-star theorem

findings.disposition: Preserve Section 2’s ordinary-import and historical-run limitations. The committed Alpha tree objection remains valid evidence about provenance, but supplies neither a counterexample nor a proof of H27. Local degree-case successes do not close this external assurance gap.
findings.statement: Citing both H27 and the prior upper-68 theorem does not provide two independent confirmations of the intersecting cap: the latter expressly imports the former.

revisions.action: Reassessed the source disclosure against fresh primary statements and the superseding tree qualification.
revisions.result: The disclosure repair remains resolved, including the correction to my earlier completeness wording; authentication itself remains unestablished.

revisions.action: Checked unchanged Section 2 against the reopened construction attribution.
revisions.result: Classical attribution remains explicit and satisfactory.

content.summary: Three skeptical challenges did not reveal a new source-scope error or invalidate the bounded comparison. H27 remains an essential, unreplayed external computation; the prior upper-68 result shares that dependency and cannot independently corroborate it. The disclosed provenance limitation remains substantive. Continued review is warranted without new required wording changes.
